title: Hedged microburst absorber and latency-aware token auction
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Introduce a combined hedging + auctioning mechanism in the prefill/decode scheduler that absorbs microbursts while letting latency-sensitive requests bid for low-latency execution windows. The goal is to decrease tail latency for latency-tier tenants without materially harming overall throughput or fairness.
background: We see recurrent 200-800ms microburst spikes from interactive customers that push prefills into large decode queues and inflate p95/p99. Existing phase-splitting heuristics focus on latency vs throughput buckets but have limited ability to absorb short bursts that overload the fast-path kernels. Separately, kernel selection is unaware of tenant utility and cannot prioritize latency-sensitive requests without risk of starving batch throughput.
proposed_solution:
Design a two-part scheduler extension:

1) Hedged microburst absorber: a short-lived local buffer that temporarily holds incoming prefill stages and releases controlled micro-slices to the runtime fabric using micro-hedging. The absorber applies kernel hints (small-seq, sparse-attn preference) to map slices to hedged fast-path kernels and reduces oscillation between fast and bulk kernels. The absorber forgoes batching briefly (50-150ms window) to protect tail latency, then merges back into normal batching when pressure subsides.

2) Latency-aware token auction: requests declare a utility vector (latency_tier: fast|standard, bid_score: 0-100) derived from tenant plans and per-request SLA. The scheduler runs a lightweight auction per micro-window: it computes a token allotment using a utility-per-cost heuristic and assigns deadline-weighted slices. Hedges are granted to winning tickets and are allowed speculative kernel reservations (soft reservations) that can be preempted with graceful fallback.

Integration notes: auction winners receive kernel-hint metadata (quantize level, prefuse KV reuse), absorber tracks KV cache affinity to avoid evicting hot prefixes. Kernel-selection hook will accept 'soft reservation id' to bias kernel placement but must still validate memory and lane constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce latency-tier p95 by >=25% on our internal interactive benchmark under 2x baseline QPS microburst traffic
End-to-end throughput drop across all tenants <=5% during steady-state (no microburst)
No tenant experiences starvation for >10s; detect and auto-recover via fallback policy
Fairness (Jain index) across tenants does not decrease by more than 0.03 compared to baseline
Canary rollout toggled via runtime flag and config: enabled per-tenant; roll back to 100% within 30 minutes if error rate rises >1.5x
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype absorber in scheduler simulation harness; add kernel-hint metadata to slice objects
Week 2: Implement auction logic (lightweight priority queue + utility scoring) and integrate with simulation; tune bidding normalization using tenant profiles
Week 3: Implement hedging and soft reservation plumbing in runtime path (kernel hint acceptance + speculative lane allocation)
Week 4: End-to-end integration QA: run microburst replay tests, KV-affinity leak checks, and stress tests on staging cluster
Week 5: Canary rollout 5% of latency-tier traffic; monitor metrics and iterate on backpressure thresholds
Post-release: collect traces to feed adaptive parameters into Redwood Optimize recommendation engine
rollout_plan: Feature guarded behind runtime flag 'microburst_absorber_v1' and tenant config 'latency_auction.enabled'. Start with internal tenants and a small set of customers on dedicated capacity. Canary for 48 hours at 5% traffic, then 24 hours at 20% if no regressions, then progressive ramp to 100% for latency-tier tenants. Auto-disable if error rate or tail latency worsens beyond thresholds defined in acceptance criteria.
metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per-tenant for prefills and decode (ms)
microburst_recovery_time (ms) — time to return to baseline p50 after spike
kernel_switch_ratio (percent of slices that moved kernel path)
test_plan: Unit tests for auction scoring, normalization, and soft-reservation expiry
Scheduler simulator tests: replay historic microburst traces and assert p95 improvements and no starvation
Staging integration: run 48-hour soak with mixed tenants, inject KV cache pressure and observe eviction patterns
Chaos test: kill a kernel worker during hedged reservation and verify fallback correctness
Performance test: measure kernel hotpath latency with and without kernel-hints to ensure no regression
tradeoffs: This design prioritizes latency-sensitive requests temporarily and therefore can slightly reduce batching efficiency. We mitigate this by making the absorber time-bounded and by allowing tenants to opt-in. Hedged reservations complicate kernel placement and may increase scheduling jitter; we control this via soft reservations and preemption policies. Complexity in billing attribution will require additional tagging work in the console.
notes: Coordinate with runtime-kernel team to accept 'kernel_hint' metadata on slice proto
Work with Console/Cost team to surface 'hedged' billing line items for observability
Potential follow-up: expose an explicit budget API so customers can programmatically set per-request bid_score
